report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of daedalus/council/vendors.py: AntigravityAdapter, OllamaAdapter, VendorAvailability, available_vendors probes. All docstring claims check out; one observation about agy probe not probing auth when signed_in asserted.
risks: available_vendors | low | agy availability probe does not verify sign-in; it trusts the operator's assertion, so a stale signed_in=True could seat a vendor that later fails auth at dispatch time. | Check whether the dispatch-time auth failure path is tested; if so, the risk is mitigated by design.

handoff.purpose: Review AntigravityAdapter, OllamaAdapter, VendorAvailability dataclass, and available_vendors probe function.

symbols.name: _auth_failure
symbols.note: Returns 'not_authenticated' if returncode is nonzero and stderr/stdout look unauthenticated; otherwise empty string.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter
symbols.note: Adapter for Google Antigravity over SSH; disabled by default unless signed_in=True; prompt via stdin, never argv.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter.__init__
symbols.note: Sets ssh_target, effort, signed_in, ssh_command, runner, endpoint; defaults lane to 'untrusted'.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter.argv
symbols.note: Builds ssh command with BatchMode, timeout, strict host key checking; agy -p - reads prompt from stdin; appends --model only if model is known.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter._dispatch
symbols.note: Returns unavailable immediately if not signed_in; otherwise runs the command and maps failures to statuses: spawn_error, timeout, not_authenticated, connect_failed, not_on_path, nonzero_exit, bad_response, or ok with parsed JSON content.

symbols.name: OllamaAdapter
symbols.note: Adapter for local or bench Ollama via native /api/chat; refuses over-budget prompts; local determined by lane_for_host.

symbols.name: OllamaAdapter.__init__
symbols.note: Sets host, output_reserve, chat, endpoint; defaults lane to 'trusted'; sets local based on lane_for_host.

symbols.name: OllamaAdapter.independence_class
symbols.note: Returns ('local', model_family(self.model)) deliberately not keyed on host.

symbols.name: OllamaAdapter._dispatch
symbols.note: Checks token count against effective input window; refuses with over_context_budget if too long; calls native_chat; maps ProviderHTTPError and timeouts to statuses.

symbols.name: VendorAvailability
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding vendor, adapter, available, reason, detail, independence_class, endpoint, lane.

symbols.name: available_vendors
symbols.note: Cheap probe: checks binaries via which, Ollama host via http_probe; no model invoked; returns tuple of VendorAvailability.

claims.text: The prompt goes on STDIN (agy -p -) and NEVER on a command line.
claims.why: argv() builds ['agy', '-p', '-'] with '-' meaning stdin; the prompt is passed via stdin_text to the runner, never on the command line.

claims.text: ssh with a trailing command does not take an argv: it concatenates its arguments and hands the string to the REMOTE login shell, which re-parses it.
claims.why: The command is constructed with ssh and a trailing '--' followed by 'agy ...'; this matches the described concatenation and remote shell parsing.

claims.text: agy has not completed its one-time interactive sign-in on this machine, so this adapter is DISABLED BY DEFAULT: it reports unavailable / not_authenticated immediately rather than hanging on an auth prompt.
claims.why: signed_in defaults to False; _dispatch returns status 'unavailable' with reason 'not_authenticated' immediately when signed_in is False.

claims.text: An operator asserts sign-in with signed_in=True; nothing here probes it, because probing means invoking a model.
claims.why: The adapter only checks the signed_in flag; no probe is performed in _dispatch or anywhere else in this chunk.

claims.text: agy -p - : '-' == read the prompt from stdin
claims.why: argv() includes '-p', '-' and the runner is called with stdin_text=text, so '-' instructs agy to read from stdin.

claims.text: The host is passed EXPLICITLY per call. OLLAMA_HOST is never read for routing and never written
claims.why: host is a constructor parameter; _dispatch passes host to native_chat; no reference to OLLAMA_HOST appears in this chunk.

claims.text: local is sensitivity.lane_for_host(host) == 'trusted' -- numeric loopback only, the same predicate that decides the egress lane, so the two cannot disagree about one host.
claims.why: self.local = lane_for_host(self.host) == 'trusted' exactly matches the claim.

claims.text: Over-budget prompts are REFUSED LOUDLY. Ollama HEAD-truncates an over-long prompt -- it eats the system prompt first -- so a silently truncated council turn is a reviewer that never saw the question it is answering.
claims.why: _dispatch computes tokens and if tokens > window returns status 'error' with reason 'over_context_budget' and an explanatory message; it does not send the prompt.

claims.text: The budget is _ollama_native.effective_input_window() (full num_ctx minus the generation reserve), reused rather than reinvented.
claims.why: _dispatch calls effective_input_window() (or with reserve) and num_ctx_value() for the message; the claim matches the code.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT keyed on host: local 7b and bench 7b are the same weights, so they must collide as one class.
claims.why: The property returns ('local', model_family(self.model)) with no host component.

claims.text: Cheap probe result. No model is invoked to produce this.
claims.why: The dataclass itself only holds data; available_vendors uses only which and http_probe, no model invocation.

claims.text: Does the binary exist; does the Ollama host answer /api/version. No model is invoked, no prompt is sent, nothing is billed.
claims.why: The function calls which for claude, codex, ssh, and http_probe for the Ollama host; no model calls are made in this function.

claims.text: agy is reported unavailable until an operator asserts sign-in: the only way to test its auth is to call it, and a probe that calls a model is not a probe.
claims.why: For agy, if ssh exists but agy_signed_in is False, reason is set to 'not_authenticated' and available is False; no auth probe is performed.

claims.text: Both callables are injectable so a test can establish availability with no CLI on PATH and no network.
claims.why: which and http_probe are parameters with defaults, allowing injection.

claims.text: ONE predicate, shared with the egress gate it feeds. Not a local copy: local and lane must never be able to disagree about the same host, and they did ([::1] was local-but-untrusted).
claims.why: self.local is computed from lane_for_host(self.host) == 'trusted', the same predicate used for lane; no separate copy exists.

observations.what: The agy availability probe trusts agy_signed_in without any verification; if the flag is stale, the adapter will be reported available but fail at dispatch time.
